How it worksMembershipsEvidenceAboutFind your Good Span

A personalised way
to make longevity part
of everyday life.

Build a six-month Good Span around what matters most to you, with practices that fit your life and change as you progress. Your Pilot, a trained human longevity guide, is there from your first conversation, and you choose how much ongoing guidance you’d like.

Find your Good Span
01

Step one

Find your Starting Position.

Begin with a free personal evaluation of your habits, priorities and everyday life across six connected dimensions: nutrition, sleep, movement, mind, connection and prevention.

Tell us what’s already working, what you’d like to improve and how much time you have. You’ll receive your Starting Position: a clear picture of your strengths, your opportunities and where it makes sense to start.

02

Step two

Build your Good Span.

Your Good Span begins with a small number of science-backed practices, chosen around your goals, current habits and available time. Some help you build something new, while others strengthen what you already do or help you do it more consistently.

See what a Good Span looks like

Every Good Span is different. Browse five example members to see how it adapts to different lives.

  • Anna, 52, school administrator

    Busy weeks have pushed sleep, meals and time with friends down her list.

    Sleep · Nutrition · Connection

    Example practices

    • SleepGet some natural light outdoors soon after you wake up, for 5 minutes, 3 days a week.
    • NutritionAdd a portion of vegetables or fruit to one meal a day, 3 days a week.
    See Anna’s Good Span

  • Claudio, 38, architect and keen cyclist

    Already active and ready to go further.

    Movement · Sleep · Prevention

    Example practices

    • MovementDo a short-interval session of about 30 minutes, including a warm-up, once a week.
    • SleepKeep your bedtime and wake time consistent every day, weekends included.
    See Claudio’s Good Span

  • Teresa, 56, going through menopause

    Her sleep has changed, and she wants to stay strong for the years ahead.

    Sleep · Movement · Mind

    Example practices

    • MovementDo a full-body strength session, using bodyweight or light weights, for 30 minutes, once a week.
    • SleepChoose a regular bedtime and keep to it every weeknight, Monday to Friday.
    See Teresa’s Good Span

  • Manuel, 68, recently retired

    Healthy habits in place, and keen to stay sharp and connected.

    Connection · Mind · Prevention

    Example practices

    • ConnectionVolunteer for a one-off task, for a couple of hours, once this month.
    • PreventionPractise a new skill that stretches you, for 1 hour, once a week.
    See Manuel’s Good Span

  • Maria, 34, busy professional

    Feels healthy, but long days leave little room to switch off.

    Nutrition · Mind

    Example practices

    • NutritionAdd a portion of vegetables or fruit to one meal a day, 3 days a week.
    • MindJoin a beginner yoga class or follow a beginner-friendly session for about 60 minutes, once a week.
    See Maria’s Good Span

These are example members, not real people.

03

Step three

Meet your Pilot.

Your six-month Good Span begins with a welcome call with your Pilot, who helps you put it into practice. Together, you review your Starting Position, talk through your recommended practices and refine them around your goals, available time and everyday life.

Ask questions, raise anything that doesn’t feel right, and agree on practices that feel realistic for you.

04

Step four

Review and adapt your Good Span.

Your Good Span changes as you put it into practice. Each month, look at what’s working, what feels difficult and what needs to change. For each practice, you can:

Continue
Keep building consistency, or keep doing what works.
Build on
Take a further step when you feel ready.
Adjust
Change how often or how you do it, so it fits your life.
Replace
Try another practice that better suits your priorities.
05

Step five

Choose your human support.

After your welcome call, choose how much human guidance you want, from focused conversations with your Pilot when you need them to regular support throughout your Good Span.

Your Pilot helps you make sense of what’s working, work through what isn’t, and adjust your practices as your life and priorities change. When deeper expertise would help, they connect you with the right specialist.

Explore memberships

What supports you.

Member App and Practice Journal

Follow your Good Span and reflect on how your practices fit into your days. Notice what’s getting easier and what you’d like to change, and bring it to your next review.

Specialists

We work with selected professionals in nutrition, sleep, movement and psychological wellbeing. Depending on your membership, consultations are included or available at preferred member rates.

Connection

Meet people who share an interest, a goal, a city or a curiosity about living well, through member introductions, Longevity Live and shared activities, with more local gatherings as our communities grow.

Quarterly Refuel

As an included benefit, Core members receive €50 and Concierge members €100 each quarter to spend on selected services and products at preferred rates, such as a sleep consultation, a light therapy lamp or an organic food basket. Your Pilot can help you choose.

06

Step six

Discover your New Position.

After six months, revisit the six dimensions and review your New Position with your Pilot. Compare it with your Starting Position to see what has changed, what has become easier and where you’d like to focus next.

Your New Position then becomes the starting point for your next Good Span, shaped by everything you’ve learned.
